i.norm: Verifies that when option "-s" (which requires an argument) is immediately followed by another option flag "-s" instead of a value, the parser throws a MissingArgumentException. The stopAtNonOption flag is set to true, but since the missing argument is detected before any non-option token, parsing still aborts with an exception.
"s" is a short option that requires an argument

args[0] = "-s" sets currentOption to "s" (awaiting its required argument) args[1] = "-s" is another option flag, not a value — triggers MissingArgumentException args[2..6] are null and are ignored by the parser
